summary: Australian reviewers see the Kona Electric as a competent, easy-to-live-with small SUV with genuinely spacious packaging and a comfortable, relaxed ride around town, backed by Hyundai's dealer network. The Extended Range base grade is widely rated the pick of the range as strong value, while the Standard Range's real-world range and slow 100kW charging are seen as behind newer rivals, and the step up to Premium is questioned as not clearly worth the extra outlay. Recent price cuts of roughly $8,000 across the range have sharpened its position against cheaper Chinese EVs without changing the fundamental verdict: a sound, unexciting choice rather than a class leader.
pros: Spacious, well-packaged interior for the class, with strong rear legroom and a rare space-saver spare wheel
Comfortable, well-damped ride that soaks up potholes and speed bumps around town
Easy-to-use dual-screen infotainment with thoughtful right-hand-drive ergonomics
Extended Range grade seen by reviewers as strong value following 2026 price cuts, undercutting the Premium by around $10,000 for similar underlying capability
cons: Standard Range's real-world range (around 350km) looks light for a modern EV, especially for interstate trips
100kW DC fast-charging trails newer 800V rivals and is described by reviewers as not great for the segment
Chassis gets bouncy and less composed at highway speed or when pushed harder
Premium trim's price premium over Extended Range is questioned as not clearly justified by the added equipment
